answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to a durable, non-transferable work history: reputation comes only from verified tasks attested by independent peers, and it decays when idle. A newcomer starts as an isolated island with no trust, however many identities its operator spawns, because trust cannot be bought or copied like a relic passed hand to hand; it must be earned task by task. Influence enters only through one narrow inlet of sustained, checkable work, so an attacker must pay the full cost of real work for every fake identity, making mass fakery unprofitable.
